description: The Garbage Free City star rating is the annual assessment of urban solid waste services under India's Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0, run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and its results are published as dashboards. The 2024-25 dashboard read on 2026-09-28 reports an assessment of 3,583 urban local bodies by 3,501 assessors, covering more than 73,000 wards and 10,806 dry and wet waste plants, of which 8,987 were functional, with over 14 million photographs and about 1.6 million citizen validations. Headline results count wards with more than 90% door-to-door collection (60,478) and source segregation (39,648), and local bodies processing at least half their wet waste (1,325) or dry waste (1,455) and having a construction and demolition waste facility (1,792). Ratings follow self-assessment, third-party verification and ministry certification valid for one year, and dashboards for the 2022 and 2023 cycles are also online. Coverage is urban India. Access is free; no licence or download was read. Caveats: figures are programme ratings built on self-reporting and verification, and city-level tables were not opened. It supports waste service capacity studies, such as locating cities whose processing capacity lags collection. No related Indian waste record is catalogued.
